context: ▶ Remark 3. In the literature, the running time of n × n matrix multiplication is typically written as O(nω ), where ω is the “exponent of matrix multiplication,” the infimum over all reals τ ≥ 2 such that n × n matrices can be multiplied in O(nτ ) time. The use of the infimum in this definition means that, technically, we can compute the product of two n × n matrices in O(nω+ε ) time for any constant ε > 0, but not necessarily in O(nω ) time. Since our work involves optimizing subpolynomial factors in the time complexity of NWT, we denote the runtime of matrix multiplication by MM(n) to avoid confusion. 1.1 Additional Related Work Vertex-weighted versions of graph problems beyond triangle detection have received more the last few years. For example, [1] proved that APSP with node weights can attention in p be solved in n3 · MM(n) poly(log n) time, even though the classic edge-weighted version of APSP is conjectured to require n3−o(1) time [14]. The classic Minimum Cut problem can be solved in near-linear time [10], but extending this result to the node-capacitated case remains open [7]. Researchers have also studied node-weighted versions of maximum matching [3] and dominating set [2]. 2 Preliminaries Throughout we let G = (V, E) denote the input graph on n vertices. All graphs we consider have vertex weights, with wt(v) denoting the weight of vertex v. We let MM(a, b, c) denote the time complexity of multiplying an a × b matrix with a b × c matrix. Let MM(n) = MM(n, n, n). We make use of the standard fact that an unweighted triangle in a tripartite graph with vertex parts X, Y, Z can be detected in MM(|X|, |Y |, |Z|) time (see e.g., the argument presented in [9, Section 5.3]).
